questions.question_text: A prism has a semicircular cross-section of diameter $12$ cm and is $9$ cm long. Find its volume in exact form, in terms of $\pi$.

options.why: Used the diameter $12$ as the radius, giving $\tfrac12\pi(12^2)$ instead of $\tfrac12\pi(6^2)$.
Used a full circle $\pi r^{2}$ for the cross-section instead of a half circle $\tfrac12\pi r^{2}$.
Stopped at the cross-sectional area and did not multiply by the $9$ cm length.

questions.solution_text:
The cross-section is a semicircle of radius $r = 6$ cm.
$A = \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 6^{2}$
$= 18\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 18\pi \times 9$
$= 162\pi\text{ cm}^{3}$

questions.question_text: A quarter-round moulding is a prism with a quadrant cross-section of radius $8$ cm, and it is $6$ cm long. Find its volume, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used a semicircle $\tfrac12\pi r^{2}$ instead of a quadrant $\tfrac14\pi r^{2}$ for the cross-section.
Used a full circle $\pi r^{2}$ instead of a quarter circle for the cross-section.
Stopped at the cross-sectional area and did not multiply by the $6$ cm length.

questions.question_text: A prism has a sector cross-section of radius $10$ cm and angle $72^{\circ}$, and it is $3$ cm long. Find its volume in exact form, in terms of $\pi$.

options.why: Used a full circle $\pi r^{2}$, ignoring the $\tfrac{72}{360}$ fraction of the sector.
Left out the length, multiplying the sector area by the angle fraction a second time.
Doubled the angle fraction, effectively using $144^{\circ}$ instead of $72^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text: A prism has a sector cross-section of radius $5$ m and angle $120^{\circ}$, and it is $9$ m long. Find its volume, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used a full circle $\pi r^{2}$, ignoring the $\tfrac{120}{360}$ fraction of the sector.
Stopped at the cross-sectional area and did not multiply by the $9$ m length.
Used a $60^{\circ}$ fraction instead of $120^{\circ}$, halving the sector area.

questions.question_text: A half-round trough has a semicircular cross-section of diameter $14$ cm and is $20$ cm long. Find its volume, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used a full circle $\pi r^{2}$ for the cross-section instead of a semicircle.
Used the diameter $14$ as the radius instead of halving it to $7$.
Stopped at the cross-sectional area and did not multiply by the $20$ cm length.

questions.solution_text:
The cross-section is a semicircle of radius $r = 7$ cm.
$A = \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 7^{2}$
$= \frac{49}{2}\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= \frac{49}{2}\pi \times 20$
$= 490\pi$
$= 1539.3804\ldots$
$\approx 1539.4\text{ cm}^{3}$

questions.question_text: A prism with a semicircular cross-section of radius $5$ cm has a volume of $175\pi$ cm³. Find its length.

options.why: Used a full circle $25\pi$ for the cross-section, so dividing $175\pi$ by $25\pi$ gave half the length.
Used a quadrant $\tfrac14\pi(5^2)$ for the cross-section, doubling the length found.
Forgot to square the radius, using $\tfrac{1}{2}\pi(5)=2.5\pi$ for the cross-section area.

questions.question_text: A prism has a semicircular cross-section of radius $4$ m and length $9$ m. A student wrote $V = \pi \times 4^{2} \times 9 = 144\pi$ m³. Which statement correctly identifies the error and the right volume?

options.text: The cross-section is a semicircle, so its area is $\tfrac12\pi r^{2}$; the volume is $72\pi$ m³.
The working is correct; the volume is $144\pi$ m³.
options.why: It uses a full circle $\pi r^{2}$, but a semicircular cross-section is only half of that.

options.text: The radius should have been halved, giving $36\pi$ m³.
options.why: The radius is already given as $4$ m; halving it would wrongly treat $4$ as a diameter.

options.text: The length was left out, so the volume is $8\pi$ m³.
options.why: The length $9$ was included; the actual error is using a full circle instead of a semicircle.

questions.solution_text:
The cross-section is a semicircle, so its area is half of $\pi r^{2}$.
$A = \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 4^{2}$
$= 8\pi\text{ m}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 8\pi \times 9$
$= 72\pi\text{ m}^{3}$

questions.question_text: A pipe is a $12$ m long prism whose inside is a semicircle of radius $2$ m and whose outside is a semicircle of radius $3$ m (a semicircular shell). Find the volume of the shell material, in m³, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used the outer semicircle alone without subtracting the inner semicircle.
Used full circles instead of semicircles for the ends, giving $\pi(3^2-2^2)\times12$.
Subtracted the radii before squaring, using $\tfrac{1}{2}\pi(3-2)^2\times12$ instead of $\tfrac{1}{2}\pi(3^2-2^2)\times12$.

questions.solution_text:
The shell cross-section is the outer semicircle minus the inner semicircle.
$A = \frac{1}{2}\pi (3^{2} - 2^{2})$
$= \frac{5}{2}\pi\text{ m}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= \frac{5}{2}\pi \times 12$
$= 30\pi$
$= 94.2477\ldots$
$\approx 94.2\text{ m}^{3}$

questions.question_text: A prism with a sector cross-section of radius $9$ cm and length $8$ cm has a volume of $54\pi$ cm³. Find the angle of the sector.

options.why: Forgot to divide by the length, using the full $54\pi$ as the cross-sectional area.
Divided by the length twice, halving the correct angle fraction.
Left $\pi$ in the arithmetic and cancelled it incorrectly against $r^{2}$.
